text:
marta: quick follow-up to the multi-region RFC. thinking about making control-plane the single source for residency decisions and emitting signed routing tokens. routers validate and enforce. pros: single audit trail, simpler router logic. cons: control-plane availability affects routing. any immediate blockers?

anika: blocker for customers with strict KMS/HSM rules. we must ensure tokens carry key-scope info and never cause cross-border decrypts. propose token fields: tenant, region, key_policy, issuer, issued_at, ttl. also need per-request attestation logs.

soren: agree on token format. runtime behavior: router checks signature -> routing header applied -> if header missing or unreachable, router falls back to operator-authored static map. add short cache TTL (20-30s) to limit stale decisions.

jeff: streaming calls are tricky. if a tenant moves regions mid-stream we must signal graceful drain and ask client to reconnect. recommend client reconnect idempotency and a short reconnect window. also need cache versioning for model KV.

ops-bot: smoke-test: token_signing ok, fallback_map exercised on simulated network partitions. logs: https://ci.example/2765432100/smoke :white_check_mark:

legal: add audit fields: requestor_id, justification_id, policy_reference. retention for cross-region key proxy calls must be explicit.

marta: next steps: i'll write a compact RFC addendum with token schema, router fallback rules, operator config snippet, and KMS options (mirror, proxy, envelope). target: prototype next sprint. if no objections, moving forward. :rocket:
